title: Design System: COLD DAY — Cold Dispatch

display.purpose: Page titles and the single leading number on a board. One per screen.

headline.purpose: Section and panel titles. Never used for body copy.

title.purpose: Record names, card titles, button labels.

body.purpose: All running text, cells, and form values.

label.purpose: Column headers, field labels, tag text, eyebrows.

code.purpose: OT codes, verification codes, coordinates, currency amounts.

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary CTA only. Reads as the control being powered.

shadows.name: accent-halo
shadows.purpose: Brand mark and the live indicator on an active map pin.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals, popovers, dropdown panels leaving the plane.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Colour and 1% scale on an active press.

motion.name: layout
motion.purpose: Sidebar collapse and drawer. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: Cold Dispatch is the night dispatch room of a refrigeration network. The console is on all night. Orders arrive, get picked up, move across the city, and close. Everything on screen answers one of three questions in under a second: what is live, what is stuck, and who is responsible for it. The world is a deep navy that never turns black. Two surfaces — a canvas and a raised plane — plus a well for anything you type into. Depth is carried by a one-pixel hairline and a tonal step, never by a drop shadow; the only light in the room is a single cyan signal that means this is live or this is interactive. Density is high and deliberate. This is a control tower, not a dashboard for showing off.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy canvas, one raised surface, one inset well. No black, no pure white text.
A single cyan accent, used on ≤10% of any screen.
Flat by default; hairlines and tonal steps instead of shadows.
Three typefaces with three jobs: display, text, data.
12 px type floor and a 700 weight ceiling, no exceptions.
Status is a tag, and the tag has a fixed position on every board.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal cyan covers at most 10% of any screen. If two things on a page are both cyan, one of them is decoration and must lose.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Color Rule
rules.body: When two regions need separating, reach for a hairline first. Colour is what you add when the border alone is not saying enough — not the other way round.

rules.name: The #64748b Ban
rules.body: #64748b and #475569 never carry text on canvas, surface, or well. On canvas they measure 3.9:1 and 2.5:1 — both under AA. Use #94a3b8, which measures 7.3:1, for anything that must be read.

rules.name: The 700 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Nothing renders heavier than 700. font-black (900) and font-extrabold (800) are banned outright — the incumbent web app uses them 74 times and the result is a screen where everything shouts.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text below 12px. The incumbent app declares 122 arbitrary sizes at 9, 10, and 11px; every one of them becomes 12px. If a label does not fit at 12px, the label is too long, not the type too big.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Space Mono is reserved for values a human compares character by character. Never for a sentence, never for a button, and never for a heading — with one exception: an uppercase eyebrow of two or three words.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If you are reaching for a shadow to separate two regions, you want a border. If you are reaching for a shadow to show that something is interactive, you want a hover background from surface-elevated.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-A-Status Rule
rules.body: The accent glow is never used on a secondary button, a card, or a hover state. It appears on the primary action and on the live indicator, and nowhere else.

dos: Do start every new surface from the three-layer stack: canvas → surface → well, in that order.
Do use the 12/14/16px trio for almost all text, and reserve Display for one element per screen.
Do give every state a tag with text in it, in a fixed column position.
Do keep the focus ring at 2px signal at 1px offset on every interactive element, including hand-rolled buttons that Tailwind's reset stripped.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion — every animation in this system has a static equivalent.
Do name what failed in an error state, and offer the retry next to it.
donts: Don't use #64748b or #475569 for text on any dark surface; they fail contrast.
Don't use font-black, font-extrabold, or any weight above 700 — the current web app does this 74 times and the hierarchy it buys is false.
Don't set type below 12px, including micro labels and chart axes.
Don't add a drop shadow to a card, a row, or a button to signal elevation or hover.
Don't put a gradient on anything, including the brand mark.
Don't ship a dark: variant. This system has exactly one appearance; a dark: prefix that never activates is dead code pretending to be a feature.
Don't use a colour-only status indicator — no bare dot, no colour-coded row without a textual state.
Don't invent a hover animation beyond a background step and a 150ms colour transition.
